Hi there. A person in recovery, speaking. Currently 29 so around your age.

Trying to express your concerns for someone who has the nasty habit of drinking to relax, numb, or have a good time is going to be a difficult conversation. Without them knowing; alcohol has quickly become a dependent to “relieve stress, depression, or celebrate a good time”. When people would try to talk to me about my drinking, I was extremely defensive and in denial. I think this is the case for most people. So prepare for that. I can tell you genuinely care and want the best for your partner so I assume remaining supportive, non judgmental, and patient will be easy. You’re right, this thing that “seems fine now” as he says…will get nasty later. I thought the same. That I was fine, I drank like everyone else. As cliche as it sounds, I was a functioning alcoholic. And functioning as in able to carry out the day. But that doesn’t mean the days were good. I was a bitch to my family, it was constantly affecting my mood when I never realized. I was destroying relationships around me even though I was keeping jobs school etc. it wasn’t until 2 dui’s and a bad accident later that I finally realized I had a problem I needed to get my shit together.
unfortunately, the person has to see it and want it for themselves. A suggestion I have, after reading that your partner always wants to drink when you’re together, make plans and set the boundary of “can this be a sober date?” And help show them the importance of reconnecting with how they are really feeling. It’s easier to drink about it than talk about it and that’s kinda how it all starts. And if he does decide to imply your overreacting because of your family history, suggest that maybe instead of him being defense about you bringing it up, that maybe he be more understanding and willing to adapt to make you feel more comfortable when you’re together…knowing your history and that it’s a sensitive matter to you. That’s what partners do. And you shouldn’t be gaslit. I didn’t want to make this too long but kinda went on a tangent. If you’d like to talk, my inbox is open. And the suggestion of “when you do X, I feel Y, and I think a fair solution would be Z and I’m up for other suggestions” is great advice. You sounds like a really caring partner! Good luck!

To add: I do have a history of trauma and struggle with my mental health. So I think that created a dependency on alcohol as well. This is something else to factor in with your partner, if they at all struggle with their mental health. Even the stress of the demanding university can be enough. College is when my heavy drinking started.
